## Historical audit: S0088, visible chunk 1 of 2

**Source for all citations:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Line numbers refer to this JSONL file. The reference and renders are not visually available to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 | Reconstruct one indoor RGB image as editable, separate SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and materials. The student’s “ship accommodation compartment” is its interpretation, not independently verified scene identity. |
| First build — student response line 3; execute line 4 | Code creates multiple assets: shell, column, three-tier bunks, benches, cabinets, chair, pipes and lamps. It groups constituent meshes, positions rails and supports, assigns colors, and attempts procedural floor bump and emissive diffusers. Grouping and coordinates do not verify physical contact. Camera is nearly level, lens 27; world and lights are initialized after realization. |
| First validation — execution_result line 5; select line 6; student request line 7 | Step 1 reports `ok: true`, saved PNG and blend; step 1 is selected and the render is supplied for comparison. The render log reports 16 samples despite code requesting 48. Successful execution is not proof of visual or geometric fidelity. |
| Revision — student response line 9; execute line 10 | Student diagnoses rear objects and lamps as too low, lockers too distant, and a right wall as occluding a recess. It moves and tilts the camera downward, advances lockers, changes the partition and bunk dimensions, and reduces lighting while retaining the 27 mm lens. These are the student’s visual judgments, not independently verified discrepancies. |
| Second validation and exploration — execution_result line 11; select line 12; student request line 13; session line 14 | Step 2 reports success and a saved render, is selected, and is supplied for another comparison. The student independently iterates from render feedback; sessions report no tool calls within the model sessions. The runner again reports 16 samples, although the program requests 64. |
| Third revision — student response line 15; execute line 16 | Student says heater and cabinets were excessively cropped and the chair hidden. It moves those assemblies, adds heater mounting rods, moves and rotates the chair by −18° around an explicit pivot, extends the right partition, and adjusts fill and floor roughness. Step 3 execution is launched; its result is not visible in this chunk. |

**Teacher input:** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or student receipt/adoption is visible in this chunk. The comparison instructions are runner/user feedback, not evidence of a teacher intervention.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Two builds formally executed successfully; the overall outcome is **unknown**, including whether step 3 completed or which build was ultimately submitted. There is no visible formal assessment of correctness, algorithm failure, empty patch, or technical interruption. Neither object names nor success flags establish object presence in the reference, accurate materials, actual part connections, chair pose, camera match, illumination, or visual improvement. Whether the changed floor and diffuser materials took effect is also unverified.

**Lessons:** Transferably, explicit parameters, grouped parts, API checks, and render-driven revisions made targeted iteration possible; execution success still requires visual and geometric validation. The particular locker, partition, chair and lighting adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not established improvements.
